title: Cryo Soft X-ray Tomography-Based Quantification of Phytoplankton Subcellular Structures
content: Phytoplankton, also known as algae, are a genetically, morphologically, and biophysically diverse group of photosynthetic microorganisms that form the basis of marine food webs and are responsible for a vast majority of marine carbon fixation [1]. To support their growth, phytoplankton must balance their access to light, which is abundant towards ocean surface, and nutrients, which are more abundant deeper in the ocean. Hence, phytoplankton are under ecological pressure to migrate vertically in the ocean according to their biosynthetic needs, and this vertical migration is predicted to have a significant impact on ocean primary production and nutrient cycles [2-5].
